summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The Dharmasastra corpus (the shared codified kernel) read via an orthodox, strict caste-prescriptive lens versus reformist or historically contextual readings. The contest is over which reading holds the legitimate authority to adjudicate practice, with each reading emitting radically different constraints and victim sets[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The statutory definition of a 'derivative work' (a fixed legal kernel) read expansively by incumbent rightsholders (maximizing enclosure/extraction) versus a narrow reading protecting transformative use and generative AI training (coordination/scaffold). The disagreement is about what the constraint actually is, not just where observers stand[cite: 2].

human_readable: The Doomsday Clock as Existential Metric
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The Doomsday Clock (a deliberately ambiguous practice-norm kernel) read as a purely objective scientific index of global vulnerability versus a normative, performative political tool designed to spur collective action. Tests how an authority structure (the Bulletin) grounds its interpretive legitimacy[cite: 2].

KERNEL CONTEST: The core analytical framework itself (the codified ontology) read as a strict, immutable structural diagnostic tool versus a malleable, rhetorical scaffold for policy advocacy. An epistemic kernel contest testing how the framework's own authority structure resists interpretive drift[cite: 2, 3].
